solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pompous official in Bear Inn in conversation

indicators.note: something said in conversation is spoken, so the words are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh is the famous bear, and an inn is a bar, giving POOH BAR

explanation.surface: A self-important official holds court in a pub called the Bear Inn, chatting away.
explanation.walkthrough: Pooh-Bah is the haughty official in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, whose name became a byword.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado's Lord High Everything Else gave his name to any self-important holder of many offices.

clue.text: Afterthought about old lady's last bunch of flowers

indicators.note: about has the postscript's letters go round the abbreviation for old

parts.note: PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

indicators.note: last takes the final letter of lady

explanation.surface: A postscript about an old woman's last floral bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A posy is a small bouquet, a little bunch of cut blooms.

clue.text: coincide in part with deliveries friend sent up

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone shares in part the parcels a friend dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is cricket's set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that partly cover or share the same ground or time are said to do this.

clue.text: Fine Scottish knight's physical strength

parts.note: braw is Scots for fine or splendid
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A splendid Scottish knight shows great bodily power.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn means muscle, hence bodily power.

clue.text: Way in which slow mover enters boundary?

definitions.text: Way in which slow mover enters boundary?

parts.words: Way in which slow mover enters boundary?
parts.note: a hedgehog, the slow mover, creeps along a line of shrubs marking a field's edge

explanation.walkthrough: The slow mover is a hedgehog; the field boundary is a hedge, and the way along it a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of bushes forming a field boundary, the habitat of the hedgehog.

clue.text: Prissy person initially rather lacking politeness

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word person

parts.note: somewhat impolite is rudish, rude with the softening suffix -ish

explanation.surface: A fussy, prim person who comes across as a little impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prissy person' reads as a noun phrase, but 'person' belongs to the wordplay and 'Prissy' alone is the adjective defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prissy is excessively proper and easily shocked, a synonym for being prim about morals.

clue.text: Vexed woman tearing into chap under pressure

indicators.note: under in a down clue sets the following letters beneath the pressure symbol

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: tearing into puts the woman inside the chap

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, a chap
Eve, the first woman

explanation.surface: An angry woman lays into a man who is already stressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeved is an informal synonym for annoyed or irritated.

clue.text: Ugly university son enters regularly after dark

indicators.note: enters puts the son's letter inside the word for every night

parts.note: nightly means happening every night, regularly after dark

explanation.surface: An unattractive student son goes out every night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but is part of the phrase meaning NIGHTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightly means unpleasant to look at, a synonym.

clue.text: Break actually taken without resistance

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the phrase for actually goes round the letter

parts.note: in fact means actually
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A rest break was really taken without any opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To infract is to break a law or rule, a formal word for violating.

clue.text: Anguish of ambassador over holiday tour of galleries?

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the ambassador's letters on top

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is an ambassador's title
an art break is a short holiday visiting galleries

explanation.surface: An ambassador grieves over a gallery-visiting trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreak is overwhelming distress or grief, a close synonym.

clue.text: Scarper, finding sheep tick in item of tack

indicators.note: in places the sheep parasite inside the piece of riding gear

parts.note: tack is horse-riding equipment, and a saddle is one item of it
a ked is a wingless fly that parasitises sheep, known as the sheep tick

explanation.surface: A rider bolts after discovering a parasite lodged in their saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for running away in a hurry; scarper is British slang for fleeing.

clue.text: Capital of industrialist originally in South Africa

indicators.note: in sets the following letters inside the abbreviation for the country
originally picks out the opening letter of industrialist

explanation.surface: A city of finance belonging to a magnate who began his career in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money in a business surface, but it is the city sense that defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria, so it is one example of a capital.

clue.text: Soldier's material preceding article in medical journal

indicators.note: in places the cloth and article inside the journal's name

parts.note: The Lancet is a leading British medical journal

indicators.note: preceding puts the fabric before the article

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen fabric
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A soldier's fabric is written up ahead of a paper in a medical journal.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British Army a lance sergeant was a corporal acting in the rank above, so a soldier of a particular rank.

clue.text: Shield English lad about to dodge church parade at last

indicators.note: about has the lad's letters go round the next ones

parts.note: a son is a lad
to cut, as in cutting a class, is to dodge it

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of parade

explanation.surface: An English boy skips church parade at the very end, shielding himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield bearing a coat of arms in heraldry.

clue.text: Eat with queen, one men must find condescending

parts.note: to sup is to eat supper or take food
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen
I is the Roman numeral for one
OR, other ranks, stands for ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Someone dining with royalty finds the company haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for 'other ranks', the enlisted soldiers as opposed to officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior manner is one that looks down on others, the same attitude as being condescending.

clue.text: Wide boy always supporting striker in court

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the following letters beneath

parts.note: a racket strikes the ball on a tennis or squash court
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A shady character is constantly backing a forward in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a small-time crook or spiv; 'court' is a sports court, not law.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs dishonest schemes, just the sort of shady character called a wide boy.

clue.text: Old coin sanctioned at first by King Edward, say.

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of sanctioned

parts.note: King Edward is a British potato variety, and tater is slang for a potato

explanation.surface: An ancient coin was authorised by a monarch named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Edward' looks royal but is a potato, a common British variety; 'say' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The stater was a gold or silver coinage of ancient Greek city-states.

clue.text: Game left over at end of table

parts.note: across means over, as in from one side to the other

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of table

explanation.surface: A game abandoned with the scores level at the end of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: American civil engineer after a new redemption period

indicators.note: after places the engineer's letters behind a and new

explanation.surface: An American engineer follows a new period for redeeming something.
explanation.definitionFit: In finance usance is the customary time allowed for paying a foreign bill of exchange.

clue.text: Doctor at bar is Middle East scholar

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A medic in a bar turns out to be an expert on the region.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabist is a specialist in Arabic language and culture, a scholar of that region.

clue.text: Unknown in top pub, a large rodent

indicators.note: in sets the unknown between the two words for top and pub

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
a bar is a pub
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Something strange in an upmarket pub, a big rodent perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The capybara of South America is the biggest living rodent.

clue.text: Joiner climbing mountain at a gentle pace

parts.note: and is a conjunction, a word that joins

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Etna is the Sicilian volcano

explanation.surface: A carpenter scales a peak slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' reads as a woodworker but is a conjunction.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Cross about theologian's disorganisation

indicators.note: about has the hybrid animal's letters go round the scholar's

parts.note: a mule is a cross between a horse and a donkey
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a theologian

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at a theologian's chaotic ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is a hybrid animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A muddle is a confused, disordered state, a synonym for disarray.

clue.text: French writer's talk with journalist grabbing a university chap

parts.note: a chat is a talk

indicators.note: grabbing has the journalist's letters clasp the following ones

parts.note: ED, editor, is the crossword journalist
Brian is any man's name standing for a chap

explanation.surface: A French author chats with a reporter who buttonholes a man from university.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIAN is simply a man's name, a common way for clues to use 'chap'.
explanation.definitionFit: François-René de Chateaubriand was a French Romantic writer and statesman, also giving his name to a steak.

clue.text: Someone like Zorba almost; do you concur?

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter

parts.note: Zorba the Greek, so someone like Zorba is a Greek

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Zorba-like figure almost fits, and if you share the view.
explanation.walkthrough: Zorba the Greek is the novel and film hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone if they share an opinion is asking whether they are of one mind with you.

clue.text: Talk about Panama, possibly

parts.note: C, circa, means about
a Panama is a type of straw hat

explanation.surface: Discussion about Panama as a possible subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal conversation.

clue.text: In Kiel it established a size of type

indicators.note: In says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A typeface size was standardised in the German port of Kiel.
explanation.definitionFit: Elite is a typewriter typeface of twelve characters to the inch, a standard type size.

clue.text: Cut limb off top of birch in woman's stock farm

indicators.note: in sets the tree's letter inside the woman's farm

parts.note: Di's, the possessive of the woman's name Di
a ranch is a farm raising livestock

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of birch

explanation.surface: Someone lops a branch from the birch on a woman's cattle farm.
explanation.definitionFit: To disbranch is an old verb meaning to sever or strip a branch from a tree.

clue.text: Possible source of Brazil's ten true reforms

indicators.note: reforms says the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A Brazilian political source discusses ten genuine reforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' reads as the country, but it is the brazil nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil nuts come from a tree, so a nut-bearing tree is where one might grow.

clue.text: Soldiers in East allowed to fire, perhaps, once

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the following letters

parts.note: to let is to allow
men are soldiers in the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops in the East are given permission to shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like a military order but is one of the four classical elements, earth, air, fire and water; 'once' marks the old belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient philosophy held fire to be one of four basic substances making up the world.
